tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification

TLS certificate verification is enabled in all builds, development builds included, and this applies from now on. For testing, the project uses self-signed certificates. HTTPS is used everywhere with no plain-text exceptions, and certificate management is already in place.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md`. It says certificate verification is on in all builds, development included, from now on. It also says tests use self-signed certificates, and that HTTPS is used everywhere with no plain-text exceptions.

It rests on three of the project's recorded decisions: #30 (verification in every build), #31 (self-signed certificates for testing) and #33 (HTTPS everywhere). Decision #30 replaced the earlier record #12, so I left out the old approach of turning verification off in development builds.

Muninn flags #30, #31 and #33 as conflicting with other active records. The conflicts are with the TLS library choice (OpenSSL in #7, Rustls in #21) and with an earlier record #13. They don't contradict the verification policy itself, so I wrote it as is. I didn't touch the library question because the doc doesn't cover it.

Muninn's heartbeat is also reporting RED: 20 hook runs started and never finished. That doesn't change the doc, but it may need checking.
